A1.justification: Both complete 19-page PDFs describe the same TokenFlow work and include Appendices A–C. Scientific text, equations, figures and tables match; pages 2–19 also render identically. The first-page changes concern the resource link and arXiv stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original TokenFlow reconstruction, multimodal understanding and image-generation experiments in Tables 2–4, plus ablations and supplementary analyses in Section 4.5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains the same original experimental results, including benchmark evaluations, ablations and appendix analyses. Their retention from v1 does not change their empirical status.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical dual encoders and codebooks, shared-index quantization, training losses, multi-scale representations, multi-step generation sampling and understanding input strategies.

E1.justification: Training and evaluation coverage is unchanged, including LAION/COYO, ImageNet, the multimodal understanding benchmarks, GenEval, DPG-Bench and the appendix evaluation using MS-COCO prompts. No dataset, task or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout the main and appendix experiments, including VQGAN/VQKD, LLaVA-1.5, LlamaGen, VAR, Show-o and EMU3 in their respective comparisons.

E3.justification: Reported data splits, resolutions, training schedules, model configurations, evaluation metrics, sampling parameters and comparison controls are identical in Section 4 and Appendices A–B.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix B retain the same codebook-size and component ablations, sampling/model-size/input-strategy studies, decoder refinement experiments, clustering analyses and semantic-teacher comparisons.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. No repeated-run or seed information, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals or significance tests are added, removed or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and qualitative examples match. Both report reconstruction rFID 0.63 at 384×384 in Table 2 and GenEval 0.55, or 0.63 with rewriting, in Table 4. Appendix results are also unchanged.

T1.justification: The distance definitions, shared-index optimization and loss formulations in Section 3.2, including Equations (1)–(4), are identical. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified tokenization, discrete-input understanding performance, reconstruction quality and efficient autoregressive generation.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations are unchanged. Appendix C retains the quantization-related gap to continuous semantic teachers and the qualification that understanding and generation were validated separately, with joint training left for future work.

D1.justification: The first-page resource link changes from byteflow-ai.github.io/TokenFlow/ to github.com/ByteVisionLab/TokenFlow, updating the access pointer to a repository. Implementation details, hardware information and Appendix A/Table 11 configurations remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish newly available code.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography are identical. Positioning relative to prior visual tokenizers and unified multimodal models, including novelty claims, is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page resource-link text and arXiv version/date stamp are updated. Scientific prose, terminology, section ordering, references and appendix structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–12 and Tables 1–11 retain identical contents, captions, structure and placement. Scientific displays and page layout are unchanged; the first-page differences are front-matter text edits.

improvement.justification: The main paper and appendices preserve the same methods, evidence, results, explanations and limitations. Updating the resource pointer and arXiv stamp does not materially change the paper's overall quality. The PDFs alone do not demonstrate improved code availability or reproducibility.
